scope: Targeted primary-literature and structural cross-check; not exhaustive. Animations are qualitative teaching models, never measured trajectories.

cases.title: Proton-coupled electron transfer
cases.explanation: Radical transfer and proton transfer are coupled but need not follow the same route. The long-range radical relay is not one proton crossing both subunits.
cases.review: 2025 turnover structures show multiple conformations; 2026 β-subunit calculations support conformational gating. A trapped 2020 structure alone does not give rate constants or proton tunneling probabilities.

structure.name: E. coli RNR · trapped engineered complex
structure.note: Cryo-EM 3.60 Å. The trapping construct uses E52Q and fluorotyrosine122 in β. This is a structural relay reference, not a native turnover movie.

cases.baseline: A reaction scheme treats electron and proton changes as separately parameterized steps, or combines them into one fitted rate.
cases.quantum: Electronic and proton coordinates are coupled. Concerted or sequential routes depend on energetics and local hydrogen-bond networks.
cases.boundary: A structure establishes geometry, not a measured nuclear tunneling probability. One should distinguish proof of a PCET reaction scheme from proof that a particular proton tunnels or that long-lived coherence drives the full radical relay.
cases.test: Combine site-specific redox substitutions, solvent isotope effects, time-resolved radical detection and calculations that compare sequential and concerted pathways.

cases.title: DNA photolyase repair
cases.explanation: Excited reduced FAD donates an electron to the lesion; bond cleavage and electron return complete the repair scheme. The structural view is already repaired.
cases.review: 2023 time-resolved CPD crystallography provides actual reaction snapshots. A 2024 ultrafast study concerns (6–4) photolyase photoreduction, a different reaction; neither is silently substituted for this fixed structure.

cases.baseline: A kinetic scheme says light activates an enzyme and a damaged base pair is restored; it leaves the electronic intermediate implicit.
cases.quantum: An excited flavin transfers an electron to a pyrimidine dimer, enabling bond splitting, followed by electron return.
cases.boundary: The existence of photolyase in one organism cannot be generalized to every species or to an effective treatment in human skin. A microscopic repair mechanism and the delivery/efficacy of a topical product are separate questions.
cases.test: Alter cofactor–lesion geometry or electronic energetics and measure both intermediate lifetimes and completed repair, controlling binding and protein integrity.

cases.title: Vision and retinal photochemistry
cases.explanation: Light prepares an excited electronic state. Nuclear torsion connects cis and trans structures through nonadiabatic dynamics; this is not tunneling through a spatial wall.
cases.review: Visual rhodopsin starts with 11-cis retinal. Recent microbial rhodopsin results often start with all-trans retinal and cannot be substituted unchanged.

structure.name: Bovine rhodopsin · experimental dark / 1 ps endpoints
structure.note: Dark-state 7ZBE and 1 ps photoactivated 8A6C retinal endpoints from the 2023 TR-SFX study. The light endpoint is aligned on chain-A Cα atoms (RMSD 0.200 Å). Intermediate animation frames are interpolations, not experimentally measured trajectories.

cases.baseline: A receptor model treats light as the input and activation as a fitted conversion rate; the chromophore pathway is hidden.
cases.quantum: A photon prepares an excited electronic state. Coupled electronic and nuclear dynamics steer retinal toward an altered geometry.
cases.boundary: The quantum character of photon absorption does not imply entangled visual perception or quantum consciousness. Different opsins have different photocycles, so this diagram is not a universal time-resolved map of every photoreceptor.
cases.test: Measure excited-state lifetimes, product yield and subsequent receptor activation after a chromophore or binding-pocket change; separate photophysics from downstream signaling.

cases.title: Photosynthetic charge separation
cases.explanation: Excitation energy and charge are different. The diagram tracks formation of a radical pair, not an electron ball travelling along every pigment.
cases.review: Multispectral 2D spectroscopy resolves charge separation; assignment of the earliest donor mixture remains system- and model-dependent.

structure.name: Photosystem II · D1/D2 structural context
structure.note: D1/D2 context with specific reaction-centre cofactors. P_D1/P_D2 Mg atoms lie 2.15 Å from D1-His198/D2-His197; Pheo A408 is on the Q_A side. The animation illustrates charge bookkeeping without asserting a unique initial donor pathway.

cases.baseline: A reaction-center rate model moves populations between excited and charge-separated states.
cases.quantum: Electronic coupling and the protein environment connect excited pigments to charge-transfer states while competing with recombination.
cases.boundary: Competing assignments of the earliest intermediates do not call the existence of charge separation into question. Nor does demonstrating a quantum charge-transfer mechanism establish that long-lived antenna coherence provides an organism-level efficiency advantage.
cases.test: Use multiple spectral observables and selective pigment perturbations to distinguish charge-transfer populations from overlapping exciton and vibrational signals.

cases.title: Excitons and resonance energy transfer
cases.explanation: A localized-rate description and an excitonic description can describe different regimes. FRET already rests on quantum coupling.
cases.review: Delocalization is not automatically long-lived electronic coherence. The highlighted pigment order is a teaching scan, not an inferred FMO transport path.

structure.note: One FMO chain is shown. BCL residue numbers are PDB identifiers, not a prescribed energy-transfer order. Halos show explanatory emphasis, not simulated populations or measured coherence.

cases.baseline: An incoherent Förster-type rate network transfers excitation populations between sites. Its rates already have a quantum origin.
cases.quantum: Coupled electronic states can be spread across pigments. Coherent evolution, disorder and environment determine when a rate limit is adequate.
cases.boundary: FRET is not a non-quantum alternative to quantum physics. Spatial delocalization does not by itself establish long-lived electronic coherence, and a quantum-state description is not proof of evolutionary advantage.
cases.test: Vary pigment separation and spectral overlap; compare measured transfer with the weak-coupling rate limit and more complete open-system models.

cases.review: 2025 microscopic simulations recover persistent coherence in their model; they do not by themselves overturn spectroscopic assignments or demonstrate an evolutionary advantage.

cases.explanation: Environmental fluctuations may aid some transport regimes and suppress others. No universal optimal noise is inferred from the crystal.
cases.review: The benchmark includes engineered quantum networks. The animation is a model comparison, not evidence that this protein has evolved to an optimum.

cases.baseline: A disordered network can trap excitation. A purely coherent model is not automatically the best transport model.
cases.quantum: Intermediate dephasing can release localization or destructive interference; excessive dephasing can impede transfer again.
cases.boundary: A demonstration in an engineered network is not proof that a protein has evolved to its optimal dephasing rate. Some transport enhancement can also occur in classical stochastic models, so the comparator must be explicit.

cases.title: Excited-state proton transfer in GFP
cases.explanation: The wild-type chromophore–water–Ser205–Glu222 network relays protons after excitation. Water248 is resolved in 1GFL; the animated hydrogen positions are illustrative.
cases.review: 2024 quantum dynamics studied a chromophore cluster over early dynamics. It is not a simulation of coherent proton motion through a cell.

structure.note: Wild-type 1GFL replaces the S65T-mutant 1EMA reference, whose Glu222 geometry interrupts this relay. The O···O separations are 2.63 Å (Tyr66–water248), 2.70 Å (water–Ser205) and 2.74 Å (Ser205–Glu222). Protons are idealized markers, not resolved hydrogens.

cases.baseline: A fluorescence cycle uses fitted rates between neutral and anionic chromophore states.
cases.quantum: Excitation reshapes proton energetics; a hydrogen-bonded pathway couples proton positions, vibrations and electronic emission.
cases.boundary: This is not proof of coherent proton conduction throughout an entire cell. Calculated populations depend on the included coordinates, potential-energy surfaces and treatment of the remaining protein.
cases.test: Combine residue substitutions and hydrogen/deuterium exchange with time-resolved infrared and fluorescence measurements, checking that the protein remains correctly folded.

cases.title: Ultrafast nucleobase photoprotection
cases.explanation: Excited-state population can return nonradiatively through coupled electronic and nuclear dynamics. This does not require an emitted photon.
cases.review: The cited thymine experiment probes ultrafast electronic conversion; isolated-base results cannot be treated as a complete duplex-DNA trajectory.
cases.baseline: A relaxation rate summarizes how an excited DNA base loses energy without emitting a photon.
cases.quantum: Coupled electronic surfaces and nuclear motion permit internal conversion; intersections between surfaces can route population rapidly.
cases.boundary: A gas-phase or isolated-base result cannot be copied unchanged into duplex DNA. Fast decay can be protective, but evolutionary selection of the exact quantum pathway is a further inference.
cases.test: Compare state-resolved lifetimes and lesion yields in matched bases, nucleosides and stacked sequences; check whether changing one pathway changes damage probability.

cases.title: Bioluminescence and chemiexcitation
cases.explanation: Chemical energy creates an excited emitter, which can radiate. The expanding photon ring is a symbol; it is not a coherence measurement.
cases.review: The bound analogue supplies active-site context. Emission spectra constrain the chemistry but do not turn an analogue crystal into an emitting intermediate.

structure.note: Thermostable Japanese firefly luciferase bound to a high-energy intermediate analogue (SLU). The crystal ligand is not emitting oxyluciferin; chemiexcitation is illustrated separately.

cases.baseline: Enzyme turnover is converted into a photon-production rate; excited-state chemistry is implicit.
cases.quantum: Reaction energy populates an excited emitter. Relaxation between electronic states releases a photon with a characteristic spectrum.
cases.boundary: Ordinary photon emission is not evidence for coherent quantum communication. Light yield, fluorescence quantum yield and overall bioluminescent reaction yield are related but distinct measures.
cases.test: Compare emitter analogues and binding-pocket variants using product analysis, spectra, photon yield and reaction kinetics, not color alone.

cases.title: Spin-selective oxygen photochemistry
cases.explanation: Triplet sensitizer energy transfer can excite triplet ground-state O₂ into singlet oxygen. Spin labels denote electronic states, not tiny classical spinning balls.
cases.review: Cellular singlet-oxygen formation and decay depend on generation site. This is photochemistry, not proof of weak-field physiological control.
cases.baseline: A photochemical kinetic model tracks sensitizer, oxygen and products without explicitly showing spin states.
cases.quantum: Excited-state energy transfer and spin selection access reactive oxygen states, including singlet oxygen, with distinct reactivity.
cases.boundary: Observed oxygen photochemistry does not establish that ordinary weak magnetic fields control cellular health. Nor does a measured singlet-oxygen yield by itself establish therapeutic safety or efficacy.
cases.test: Use specific detection, sensitizer-free and oxygen-dependent controls, scavenger comparisons, and localized damage readouts; distinguish singlet oxygen from other ROS.

cases.title: DNA charge transport and repair search
cases.explanation: DNA-mediated redox communication is distinct from sliding or diffusion. The duplex here contains no repair enzyme or metal cluster.
cases.review: Specific repair-protein assays support charge-transport models. A canonical duplex alone does not establish an in-cell wire network.

structure.note: Canonical DNA duplex, without repair proteins or a measured rare tautomer. It is not the experimental DNA monolayer used in spin-filtering measurements.

cases.baseline: Repair proteins find lesions by diffusion, binding and local scanning of DNA.
cases.quantum: Charge transport through stacked bases can connect redox-active proteins. Disruptions to stacking may interrupt a proposed redox search signal.
cases.boundary: These findings do not establish a universal DNA “wire network” in a living nucleus. The relative contribution compared with diffusion and sliding, and the physiological redox partners, must be established for each system.
cases.test: Perturb redox competence without eliminating lesion recognition; compare search and repair kinetics on intact versus stacking-disrupted DNA and then in cells.

cases.review: 2022 open-system calculations and mismatched-base experiments concern different systems. Neither directly gives a human mutation fraction.

structure.name: B-DNA dodecamer · structural context

cases.baseline: Rare base states, polymerase selectivity and repair determine errors; thermal chemistry can generate alternative proton positions.
cases.quantum: Proton tunneling may alter rare-state populations or lifetimes. A state must then be captured during copying and escape correction.
cases.boundary: The modeled canonical G–C transfer problem and the experimentally probed mismatched-base states are not the same experiment. A predicted tautomer population cannot be reported as the fraction of human mutations caused by tunneling.
cases.test: Combine isotope-sensitive state measurements with polymerase assays and mutation sequencing, controlling replication speed, damage, selection and repair.

cases.title: Proton wires, channels and pumps
cases.explanation: Grotthuss transport redistributes covalent bonds and charge through waters; the same proton need not cross the entire channel.
cases.review: The quantum-classical calculation treats a water dimer embedded in gramicidin. It is not a measured full-channel proton wavefunction.

structure.name: Gramicidin A · membrane-channel reference
structure.note: Solid-state NMR channel structure. No water chain or moving proton is resolved here. The adjacent wire is idealized; proton hopping does not mean one nucleus traverses the entire wire.

cases.baseline: Hydrogen-bond rearrangements and an electrochemical gradient drive proton conduction in a rate or molecular-dynamics model.
cases.quantum: Explicit nuclear motion changes zero-point distributions, sharing and possible tunneling along short hydrogen-bonded segments.
cases.boundary: A calculated short-segment effect does not prove coherent conduction along a whole channel, much less throughout mitochondria. Passive conduction, active pumping and ATP-synthase rotation are distinct functions.
cases.test: Compare isotope effects, conductance and calculated free energies across controlled channel variants; quantify whether quantum treatment improves predictions beyond uncertainty in solvation and structure.

cases.title: Quantum proposals for ion channels
cases.explanation: Classical knock-on describes interacting ions and coordination. The alternative quantum panel is a proposal, not a demonstrated extra route through this structure.
cases.review: The 2026 tunneling argument is a preprint; high flux and selectivity alone do not distinguish it from classical mechanisms.

structure.name: KcsA · one crystallographic protomer
structure.note: One KcsA protomer and crystal K⁺ sites, with Fab omitted. The full tetramer is not reconstructed. Site occupancy in a crystal is not a direct movie of permeation.

cases.baseline: Electrostatics, selectivity-filter geometry and correlated knock-on motion generate rapid ionic conduction.
cases.quantum: Some models propose tunneling or coherent ionic states across filter barriers. Predictions depend strongly on barrier and bath assumptions.
cases.boundary: Fast transport and ion selectivity are not unique signatures of quantum coherence. Uncertainty about water occupancy or a detailed classical mechanism does not establish an alternative quantum proposal.
cases.test: Derive discriminating isotope, temperature or field predictions from realistic structures, then test them against equally calibrated classical-nuclear simulations and electrophysiology.

cases.explanation: Nuclear-spin isotope effects require a suitable spin-dependent chemical mechanism. Mass effects and isotope purity are separate controls.
cases.review: A creatine-kinase reexamination found no enhancement under its tested conditions; claims of universal ATP-production enhancement are not warranted.

cases.title: Fröhlich modes and vibrational proposals
cases.explanation: Mode condensation can occur in a driven classical nonlinear model. Concentration of energy and quantum coherence are not synonyms.
cases.review: The 2018 optically driven protein experiment explicitly includes a classical explanation; it does not establish a metabolically maintained quantum state.
cases.baseline: Driven, damped classical oscillators can synchronize or concentrate energy in a low-frequency mode.
cases.quantum: Fröhlich-type models propose nonequilibrium mode condensation; stronger versions require persistent quantum coherence. Davydov-type ideas instead propose self-trapped vibrational energy.
cases.boundary: These results do not show that ordinary metabolic pumping creates a long-lived quantum coherent state in living tissue. Classical nonlinear dynamics can supply alternative explanations for some collective observables.
cases.test: Measure phase-sensitive observables, pumping thresholds, mode populations and coherence times against a matched classical model, then establish the energy source and causal cellular function.

cases.title: Xenon isotope effects in anesthesia
cases.explanation: An isotope-associated animal endpoint does not identify a molecular spin mechanism. The radical pair in the model remains a proposal.
cases.review: The 2021 radical-pair model can fit a pattern but does not uniquely establish causal chemistry or a basis for consciousness.
cases.baseline: Anesthetic action depends on molecular interactions, exposure and network physiology; isotope-associated differences can have several causes.
cases.quantum: A proposed radical-pair pathway uses xenon nuclear spin to alter reaction dynamics and, indirectly, an anesthetic endpoint.
cases.boundary: The animal endpoint does not identify the proposed radical, show coherent neural computation or demonstrate the physical basis of consciousness. Fitting an isotope pattern does not establish unique causality; replication and mechanistic controls remain essential.
cases.test: Replicate blinded isotope-dose comparisons with exposure controls; detect and perturb the candidate radical pathway while measuring the same anesthetic endpoint.

cases.title: Posner molecules and nuclear-spin cognition
cases.explanation: The diagram follows a hypothetical chain. It is not a measured neuronal structure or an observed calcium-phosphate quantum register.
cases.review: Spin-dynamics calculations test idealized clusters; no measured brain coherence time is inferred from those calculations.
cases.baseline: Calcium chemistry, ion channels and synapses transmit neural signals without invoking protected nuclear-spin information.
cases.quantum: The proposal uses phosphorus nuclear spins in calcium-phosphate clusters as protected information carriers, with chemistry linking spins to signaling.
cases.boundary: Phosphorus having nuclear spin is established physics; the proposed biological information architecture is not. An upper-bound lifetime from an idealized model must never be described as a measured neuronal coherence time.
cases.test: First identify the proposed cluster species and lifetimes in the relevant medium. Then directly test state preparation, nonclassical correlations and a selective, reproducible biochemical readout.

cases.title: Orchestrated objective reduction
cases.explanation: Tubulin is real; the proposed sequence connecting it to consciousness is not experimentally established. Animation does not upgrade evidence.
cases.review: Optical measurements of tubulin do not test the full Orch OR chain. Competing decoherence estimates are theoretical constraints, not observations of cognition.

structure.name: α/β tubulin · taxol-stabilized sheet structure
structure.note: A tubulin dimer from zinc-induced sheets, not a complete microtubule or neuron. Tryptophan positions are measured; collective-state lifetimes and consciousness claims are not encoded in them.

cases.baseline: Neural activity is modeled through molecular signaling, electrophysiology and network dynamics; consciousness remains an explanatory challenge.
cases.quantum: Orch OR proposes organized microtubule quantum states and a further objective-reduction process connected to conscious events.
cases.boundary: Recent microtubule optical experiments do not test the entire Orch OR chain. Neither a failure of one decoherence estimate nor an unresolved question in consciousness establishes the alternative theory.
cases.test: Define a uniquely predicted molecular observable and timescale; demonstrate selective coherent manipulation under physiological conditions and a causal cognitive effect that established physiology does not explain.

cases.title: Spin selection and biological handedness
cases.explanation: The experiment concerns an RNA precursor crystallizing on a magnetic surface. Opposite shapes are enantiomer labels, not an atomistic reconstruction.
cases.review: The 2023 result is a laboratory symmetry-breaking route. It is not a complete reconstruction of biological homochirality.
cases.baseline: Stereochemistry, asymmetric catalysis, crystallization and amplification can enrich one molecular handedness.
cases.quantum: A spin-polarized magnetic surface interacting with chiral molecules can bias selection in a proposed CISS-related route.
cases.boundary: An enriched precursor is not a living system or a complete explanation of amino-acid and sugar handedness. The prevalence of suitable environments and integration with plausible prebiotic networks remain open.
cases.test: Test opposite magnetic orientations, opposite handedness, nonmagnetic controls and independent replication; then examine compatibility with realistic mixtures and downstream synthesis.

cases.title: Ultraweak photons and neural communication
cases.explanation: Emission is measured in biology, but a functional neural communication channel is a separate claim. The propagating symbol is hypothetical in that context.
cases.review: The cited axon-waveguide calculation is theoretical; neither targeting nor entanglement is established by rare-photon detection alone.
cases.baseline: Oxidative chemistry can emit rare photons as a byproduct; neurons communicate through established electrochemical pathways.
cases.quantum: Proposals add guided photon signaling along axons; a still stronger version asks whether photons could carry quantum correlations.
cases.boundary: Biological light emission is not proof of targeted communication, coherence, entanglement or consciousness. An apparatus that detects rare photons measures emission; it does not automatically identify their functional role.
cases.test: Demonstrate source-to-receiver transfer with physiological photon budgets and a causal signaling consequence; only then test whether a genuinely nonclassical observable is required.

cases.title: Engineered protein quantum sensors
cases.explanation: Applied fields and radio-frequency excitation modulate a spin-sensitive fluorescence signal. This is an engineered sensor experiment.
cases.review: 2026 MagLOV demonstrates room-temperature cellular ODMR. The parent scaffold is shown; cryogenic EYFP coherent-control results are a distinct experiment.

structure.name: AsLOV2 · parent scaffold for MagLOV
structure.note: Parent LOV2 fold with FMN, not the engineered MagLOV2 variant. The 2026 sensing study uses this scaffold as structural context. No native qubit or Earth-field compass is implied.

cases.baseline: A conventional fluorescent reporter reads intensity, color or lifetime as a function of its chemical environment.
cases.quantum: Spin preparation or resonance changes an optical signal, adding magnetic/radiofrequency addressability and spin-sensitive sensing.
cases.boundary: Cold coherent-control results must not be described as physiological qubit lifetimes. MagLOV resonance under applied fields is not proof of an Earth-field animal compass or a ready clinical sensor.
cases.test: Quantify sensitivity, calibration drift, phototoxicity, targeting, perturbation and cross-sensitivity in the intended cellular environment, with conventional reporters as controls.
